evidence.producer: PROVISIONAL: src/target/backend.c registers five explicit Core/Module→machine emit backends. One sealed Core function and ModuleIR graph feeds target-specific physical ABI planners, frame selectors, ISA opcode selectors and GNU assembler producers; none may reconstruct mutable C AST state.
consumers: src/target/riscv/machine_core_select.c and machine_core_select.h are a REAL shared RISC-V RV32I/RV64I Core→typed MachineIR selector. Machine plan borrows either independently finalized RV32 ILP32 ABI or RV64 LP64/LP64D ABI and physical frame; shared instruction selection is not a shared physical ABI.

src/target/riscv32/rv32_emit.c, rv32_abi_plan.h own RV32 XLEN=32-word outgoing and incoming arguments, stack-word sizes, two-word scalars, variadic register-save and ILP32 physical frame; use shared machine selector through explicit abi32 plan.

src/target/riscv64/codegen_function.c and function_abi_plan.h own RV64 LP64 vs LP64D GPR/FPR transport, sret, frame/callee-save and finalized per-call plan; use shared selector through abi64 function view with independent offsets and runtime libcall requirements.

src/target/aarch64/codegen.c owns AAPCS64 8 GP+8 FP argument registers, x8 indirect return, dedicated ABI variadic state and its own NEON / source ASM admission; uses common DirectLP64 function lifecycle but ISA-specific selector and policy.

src/target/loongarch64/codegen.c owns LP64D aggregate split/first-GPR indirect return, contiguous variadic cursor, LP64S soft-float admission and LoongArch-specific source ASM/opcode; the DirectLP64 shared emitter is parameterized by a distinct target-owned policy.

src/target/x86_64/codegen.c and abi.h own SysV vs Win64 register banks, extra callee-saved registers and x86-specific provenance/relocation semantics; x86 cannot use the A64/Loong physical ABI merely because it is a 64-bit target.

src/target/common/machine_production_preflight.h and common/direct_function_emit.h own whole-function verified MachineIR preflight before any function body text; target-specific validation and relocations remain distinct.
evidence.functional_path: C07 PROVISIONAL five-target machine ownership graph: backend catalog picks only the registered architecture implementation -> sealed Core/Module facts arrive from common visitor -> each ISA constructs its own immutable ABI classification, stack/GPR/FPR/variadic frame, callee-save and source-ASM eligibility -> architecture selector produces complete typed MachineIR -> target ISA/opcode and GNU ASM policy verified with whole-function preflight -> machine body emission. Shared RISC-V selector resides in src/target/riscv/ and is consumed by RV32 ILP32 and RV64 LP64(D) programs from their own independent abi32/abi64 plans. AArch64 and LoongArch share DirectLP64 orchestration, not sret/aggregate/va_list policy. x86 SysV/Win64 stays separate. No ISA correctness has been certified by this mapping.
limitations: UNTRUSTED C07 MAPPING_PROPOSED ONLY. Neither every machine selector branch, GNU-ASM constraint, ABI edge case nor target differential runtime test was executed in this scout pass.

S0 V3 originally mischaracterized src/target/riscv/ as nonexistent and excluded it; V4 explicitly corrected that in durable historical event order. Future agents must inspect all shared/riscv32/riscv64 real paths, not trust old hints.

Retention of independent ABI code is legitimate even when wrappers, control flow and opcode families are similar; removing a fast path requires whole function input-output and performance equivalence.
ISA/QEMU/ELF evidence has independent per-target gates. Passing -S alone, GNU assembly alone or one target runtime never proves the other four architectures.
Need independent challenge of RISC-V shared xlen paths and private ABI cursor/frames, A64 vs Loong DirectLP64 policy and x86 SysV/Win64 before any root-cause cluster is confirmed.
